title: named_session live retrofit lacks zero-adoption path for alias-backed pool sessions
body:
## Summary
Retrofitting `[[named_session]] mode="always"` onto an already-live pool-style singleton agent does not appear to support zero-recycle adoption when the live bead has the desired alias/template but a non-canonical runtime `session_name`.

This bit the `gt` fleet on 2026-07-08 while trying to exempt long-lived leads from the session-create budget: adding named sessions for live agents (`paul`, `freya`, `data`, `amundsen`, `gandalf`) made `gc session peek <lead>` / `gc mail send <lead>` fail with `configured named session conflict ... via live bead <id>`. Reverting the config restored stability without session loss.

## What I verified in source
Current code supports adoption only for already-canonical / previously-tagged cases, not the alias-backed live-pool case:

- `cmd/gc/session_beads.go:1068-1095` indexes open sessions by `metadata.session_name`.
- Configured named desired state is keyed by the canonical named runtime session name, so a live pool-style bead with `session_name=gt-wisp-...` is not found as the desired named session.
- `cmd/gc/session_beads.go:242-263` (`canRebindConfiguredNamedSession`) allows rebinding a non-named bead only when it was previously tagged with the identity, or when backing template matches AND `session_name` equals the canonical runtime name / older identity runtime name. It does **not** allow alias-only adoption.
- `internal/session/named_config.go:369-378` then treats `alias == identity` as a conflict candidate, and `cmd/gc/session_resolve.go:76-78` surfaces that as `configured named session conflict`.
- Existing coverage (`TestSyncSessionBeads_AdoptsCanonicalSessionNameBeadIntoConfiguredNamedSession`) covers canonical-session-name adoption, not adoption of a live pool session whose only match is alias/template.

## Operational conclusion
For now, `gt` should **not** retry live `named_session` retrofits expecting zero context loss. The safe procedure is a graceful handoff-first recycle into the named-session config, or an upstream feature that explicitly adopts/renames the live runtime session and proves the metadata/runtime-name invariants.

A metadata-only retag looks unsafe: once a bead is marked configured-named but still carries a non-canonical `session_name`, reconcile has separate reconfigured-named-session handling that expects canonical runtime names, and tools use `session_name` to address the live runtime.

## Desired behavior / acceptance sketch
Either:

1. Document and guard the current limitation clearly: live pool-style sessions cannot be zero-adopted into configured named sessions unless their `session_name` is already canonical; require graceful recycle.

or

2. Add a real adoption path with tests for a live bead like:
   - `alias=paul`
   - `template=paul` / `agent_name=paul`
   - `session_name=gt-wisp-...`
   - no `configured_named_session` metadata
   - new config adds `[[named_session]] template="paul" mode="always"`

   The test should prove `gc session peek paul` resolves, no duplicate named bead is created, and runtime addressing still points to a real live session. If runtime rename is required, the test should prove the rename or graceful recycle path rather than only metadata changes.

## Related local bead
`gt-k9ghu` in the `gt` city tracks the operational consult.

title: Recover orchestration overhead of ~25% of formula-run wall clock: measured 3h35m profile
body:
## Summary

We instrumented and profiled a complete `build-from-requirements` formula run end-to-end (every bead, session, event, transcript, usage fact, trace, and git ref), reconstructed the full timing picture, and modeled where the wall clock goes. **57% of the run was actual implementation work; the rest was orchestration — and the single largest recoverable cost is a ~70–180 second dispatch tax paid at every step transition.** This issue presents the measured profile first, then the platform-layer findings, each grounded in specific code paths and constants. The companion tooling proposal is #3925.

## The run

`gc sling gc.run-operator <anchor> --on build-from-requirements` on a greenfield rig (simple todo app; 15-step main chain, 9-work-item implementation drain via per-item `do-work` sub-workflows). Result: approved build, zero blocking review findings. Profile reconstructed from the durable city event log, bead timestamps, session beads, transcripts, and `bd history`. All times UTC, 2026-07-03.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Total wall clock (sling → root close) | **3 h 35 m (215.3 min)** |
| Implementation drain (actual coding) | 123.4 m (57 %) |
| Agent sessions spawned | 36 (20 run-operator plumbing sessions) |
| Cumulative session time | 570 m (2.6× wall clock) |
| Main-chain dispatch waits (bead ready → session working) | 18.8 m, **~70–180 s at every transition** |
| Drain per-item wrapper overhead | ~4–6 m × 9 items (e.g. WI-02: 148 s ready→spawn, 133 s close-tail) |
| "Validate" steps' LLM time | 15.4 m across 5 steps (one 27-line validate step: 9 m, 35 tool calls) |
| Publish no-op (`push=false`, knowable at launch) | 2.8 m incl. a dedicated publisher session |

## The measured profile

### Main chain — where each phase's time went

Red = dispatch wait (step ready → claiming agent working). Blue = step active.

![Main-chain phase Gantt: wait vs active per phase](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/gascity/profile-assets-3924/fig1-main-chain-gantt-v2.png)

| # | Phase | Window (UTC) | Duration | Active step time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Launch + validate requirements inputs | 18:20:24–18:22:46 | 2.4 m | 1.2 m | 73 s dispatch wait first |
| 2 | Produce requirements (formalize artifact) | 18:22:46–18:34:10 | 11.4 m | 9.9 m | requirements-planner session |
| 3 | Validate plan inputs + produce implementation plan | 18:34:10–18:47:46 | 13.6 m | 1.9 m + 8.4 m | design-author session |
| 4 | Review implementation plan | 18:47:46–18:53:58 | 6.2 m | 4.6 m | review-synthesizer |
| 5 | Validate decompose inputs + create convoy | 18:53:58–19:07:53 | 14.0 m | 1.2 m + 9.5 m | task-decomposer; 9 WI beads created |
| 6 | Validate implementation convoy | 19:07:53–19:13:07 | 5.2 m | 2.2 m | 182 s dispatch gap before it |
| 7 | **Implementation drain (all coding)** | 19:13:07–21:16:33 | **123.4 m (57 %)** | see below | 9 do-work sub-workflows |
| 8 | Validate review inputs | 21:16:33–21:27:05 | 10.5 m | 9.0 m | longest "validate" step by far |
| 9 | Code review | 21:27:05–21:45:25 | 18.3 m | 17.0 m | verdict: approved, 0 blocking |
| 10 | Repair gate (no-op: nothing to fix) | 21:45:25–21:47:44 | 2.3 m | 1.2 m | |
| 11 | Finalize continuation result | 21:47:44–21:52:52 | 5.1 m | 4.4 m | |
| 12 | Publish (no-op: push=false, open_pr=false) | 21:52:52–21:55:38 | 2.8 m | 1.5 m | dedicated publisher session spawned to do nothing |
| 13 | Workflow finalize + root close | 21:55:38–21:55:45 | 0.1 m | | |

### Agent fleet — 36 sessions across the run

One bar per session (spawn → close), grouped by role. Blue = implementation workers, orange/yellow = run-operator plumbing, violet = specialists, gray = control dispatcher.

![Agent session swimlanes by role](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/gascity/profile-assets-3924/fig2-session-swimlanes.png)

| Role | Sessions | Total session time |
|---|---|---|
| core.control-dispatcher | 1 | 215.9 m (spans the run) |
| gc.implementation-worker | 9 | 173.9 m |
| gc.run-operator (plumbing) | 20 | 111.3 m |
| specialists (planner, author, decomposer, reviewers, publisher) | 6 | 68.6 m |

### Implementation drain — item segment vs actual worker time

Gray = the work item's wall-clock segment; blue = its worker session. The difference is per-item orchestration overhead (prepare/finalize operator steps + dispatch + merge).

![Drain detail: work-item segments vs worker sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/gascity/profile-assets-3924/fig3-drain-detail.png)

Sequential foundations (WI-01→03) consumed 69.1 m; the five parallel feature flows finished in 24.8 m of wall clock (≈96 m of summed worker time — parallelism bought ≈3.9×); the acceptance pass added 27.5 m. Every item's segment exceeds its worker session by ~4–6 m of wrapper overhead.

### Projected wall clock if the recommendations were applied

Modeled span-by-span against the measured data with explicit rules (dispatch gap → 25 s assuming push-wake + warm resumed session; deterministic validate/gate steps → 30 s script gates; per-item wrapper → 90 s; publish pruned; worker LLM time held fixed):

| Scenario | Wall clock | Δ |
|---|---|---|
| Measured | 3 h 35 m (215.3 m) | — |
| Conservative (rules above) | 2 h 50 m (170.0 m) | **−21 %** |
| Aggressive (+ same-session continuation groups, schema scaffolding) | 2 h 42 m (161.9 m) | **−25 %** |

Stated caveats: the 25 s floor is an engineering estimate (wake-socket ~0.2 s + nudge quiescence 3 s + observed ~20 s claim turn), not yet measured; the model composes fixes linearly (no queuing/contention model); the ~140 m of LLM working time that remains is untouched by all of these — that term is methodology-pack shaped, not platform shaped. Projected savings split roughly half platform/config (items 1–4 below) and half formula/pack.

## Platform findings

### 1. The wake-on-unblock path is a tick-polled shell order, not a push (largest cost)

`cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close` is declared `trigger = "event"` but is evaluated only when the controller ticks (patrol default **30 s**, `internal/config/config.go:2376`), where it forks `gc events --since 5m`, `gc bd dep list`, and `jq` per closed blocker/dependent, then delivers a `wait-idle` nudge (`internal/bootstrap/packs/core/orders/cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close.toml`, `.../assets/scripts/cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close.sh`, `cmd/gc/order_dispatch.go:549-583`). Meanwhile a sub-second push mechanism already exists: the nudge wake socket (`~200 ms` dial, `cmd/gc/nudge_dispatcher.go:23-44`).

**Implementation:**
- New controller component (Go): a `bead.closed` watcher inside the city runtime, subscribed via `events.Provider.Watch(ctx, afterSeq)` (250 ms file-tail under the hood, `internal/events/recorder.go:460` — vs the 30 s patrol). On each close: `store.DepList(blocker, "up")`, filter dependents `open`/`deferred` with an assignee, deliver through the existing queue (`internal/nudgequeue`) and `pingNudgeWakeSocket` (`cmd/gc/nudge_dispatcher.go:32`), which the supervisor-mode dispatcher already coalesces (`cmd/gc/city_runtime.go:744-747`).
- Wire-up beside the existing wake listener in `cityRuntime` construction (`startNudgeWakeListener`, `nudge_dispatcher.go:51`).
- Idempotency moves off the shell state file and onto queue item identity, recording "handled" only from terminal queue state — which also resolves the dedup hazard in #3929.
- Demote `cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close.sh` to a lookback safety net during burn-in; delete after.

**Acceptance:** with a warm operator, bench-nullop (profiler pack, gastownhall/gascity-packs#158) p50 sequential-step transition < 10 s (measured today: ~70–180 s); zero missed wakes across a long chain; the shell order delivers zero primary nudges during burn-in.

### 2. Two correctness hazards in the cascade path (found while profiling)

Split out as #3929: the at-most-once dedup records success when a nudge is merely *queued*, so a dead-lettered nudge permanently swallows the dependent's wake-up (until the 1 h dedup retention); and dependents with no assignee are silently skipped.

### 3. Session spawn pays a fixed multi-stage cost, and its phase timings aren't durable

Each cold spawn runs PreStart (worktree add + skills materialization + MCP config projection **under a cross-process flock**, `internal/materialize/mcp_project.go:144` — concurrent spawns serialize), a best-effort 30 s wait-for-command, a 5–60 s ready probe (`internal/runtime/tmux/adapter.go:781-789,1174-1255`), and a `gc prime` hook subprocess. This run cold-spawned 20 run-operator sessions (111 m of session time) for prepare/validate/finalize plumbing.

The spawn-phase breakdown is already computed (`startPhaseTimings`, `cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go:216`) but only emitted as a log line that `gc perf` scrapes by regex (`cmd/gc/cmd_perf.go:117`).

**Implementation (a) — durable spawn-phase event:**
- Add event type `session.spawn_phases` to `internal/events/events.go` (+ `KnownEventTypes`) with a payload struct mirroring `startPhaseTimings` (start_call / zombie_recycle / state_sync_recovery / post_start_observe / commit_refresh, total, template) in `internal/events/payloads.go`; register in `internal/api/event_payloads.go`.
- Emit where the log line prints today (`cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go`, end of `runPreparedStartCandidate`), stamping `SessionID` and — when the spawn is for routed work — `RunID` via `beadmeta.ResolveRunID`.
- Keep the log line; `gc perf`'s regex scraper (`cmd/gc/cmd_perf.go:117`) migrates to the event later.

**Implementation (b) — warm floor for plumbing roles:**
- Config already exists (`min_active_sessions`, `wake_mode` — `internal/config/config.go:616,3327`). Document the pattern for high-churn roles; consider defaulting `fallback = true` role templates to a warm floor of 1; add a `gc doctor` hint when a template shows repeated retire→respawn churn within a run.

**Acceptance:** (a) a profiled run reports spawn-phase breakdown per session from events alone; (b) a rerun of the motivating formula with the warm floor shows run-operator cold spawns ≤ 2 (measured today: 20).

### 4. No expansion-time pruning of knowable no-op steps

The publish step spawned a dedicated session for 2.8 m to conclude "`push=false` → do nothing." Both `push` and `open_pr` are formula vars known at instantiation (`stampGraphV2RootMetadata`, `internal/sling/sling.go:1462`).

**Implementation:**
- Add optional `when = "<expr>"` to `[[steps]]` (`Step` in `internal/formula/types.go`), evaluated at compile time against launch vars — the vars are already in hand at `CompileWithoutRuntimeVarValidation` (`internal/formula/compile.go:47`) when `InstantiateSlingFormula` runs (`internal/sling/sling.go:1262`).
- Keep the expression language minimal: string equality/inequality over rendered vars (`when = '{{push}} == "true" || {{open_pr}} == "true"'`); no general templating.
- Pruning must rewire the graph: dependents of a pruned step inherit its `needs` (transitive bypass) — implement in the recipe graph pass (`internal/formula/graph.go`, alongside `applyGraphControls`, which already computes sinks and would otherwise wire `workflow-finalize` to a hole).
- First consumer: the gascity pack's publish step.

**Acceptance:** a `push=false, open_pr=false` run materializes no publish bead; the workflow closes with an identical outcome; a formula with a pruned mid-chain step preserves dependency ordering end-to-end.

### 5. `events.Filter` can't select a run

`events.Event` already carries `RunID`/`SessionID`/`StepID` (`internal/events/events.go:251`) but `events.Filter` (`internal/events/reader.go:17`) has no `RunID` field, and not all record sites stamp it. Selecting one workflow's events requires a subject-set join.

**Implementation:**
- Add `RunID string` to `events.Filter` (`internal/events/reader.go:17`) and `matchesFilter` (`reader.go:53`); expose as `--run` on `gc events` (`cmd/gc/cmd_events.go`).
- Audit `Recorder.Record` call sites (`cmd/gc/api_state.go`, `cmd/gc/dispatch_runtime.go`, `internal/runproj/fold.go`, and the session lifecycle emitters) to stamp `Event.RunID` via `beadmeta.ResolveRunID(metadata, selfID, fallback)` (`internal/beadmeta/runid.go:25`) wherever a bead or session context is available — the same resolution `usage_compute.go` already uses for facts.

**Acceptance:** `gc events --run <root>` on the motivating run returns the same 2,095-event set the profiler pack's subject-set join produces from the reference capture.

### 6. Observations that are pack-layer, noted for completeness

The remaining findings are methodology-pack issues rather than platform: one-fresh-session-per-step for deterministic plumbing steps, LLM-based validation of deterministic conditions (the 9-minute validate re-derived the whole graph for a 27-line step description; `[steps.check] mode="exec"` already exists), and byte-identical 237-line priming prompts across all 12 roles. We're addressing those on the pack side; they're listed here because the projected savings split roughly half platform (items 1–4) and half pack.

### Suggested implementation order

5 and 3(a) first — small, mechanical, and they make every subsequent fix measurable per run. Then 1 (the dominant latency term). 4 is the only formula-language change and can trail. 3(b) is config/docs and can ship anytime. #3929 falls out of 1's idempotency change.

## Methodology / reproducibility

All numbers derive from durable sources keyed by the workflow root bead id: the city `events.jsonl` (ms-precision `bead.*`/`session.*` with full payloads), bead timestamps + `bd history`, session beads (spawn/close), provider transcripts (per-turn), `usage.jsonl`, and git. The full reference capture (110 beads + history, 36 session beads, 38 transcripts, a 39,827-event slice, timing model, and the HTML report these figures come from) exists and can be shared; #3925 proposes packaging this as a reusable profiler (v0 implementation: gastownhall/gascity-packs#158). Figures hosted on the `profile-assets-3924` branch.

title: Make status bead reads cancellable via ContextLister
body:
## What this changes

Status and API read paths can now cancel slow bead `list` calls through a `ContextLister` capability instead of returning to the caller while the backing `bd` process keeps running. **All** production status store shapes — city, rig, and their controller-scoped variants — are wired with a context-aware runner, so on a per-store timeout the backing `bd` child is actually canceled and its connection released, across the real construction paths used by `gc status` and the status API handlers.

The native doltlite read path has a matching `ListContext`, and `statusListStoreWithTimeout` keeps a goroutine+select guard around the `ContextLister` branch so an implementation that cannot honor ctx (a nil-runner `BdStore` fallback, or the synchronous native SQLite scan) still returns the caller at the deadline. The context-aware runners resolve env with managed-Dolt recovery disabled, so a stuck backend cannot spend the caller's whole ~1s status budget in `recoverManagedBDCommand` before the subprocess even spawns. The temporary scoped-store mitigation that main used for bounded status reads is removed because the ContextLister path supersedes it at the same call sites.

Originating architecture decision: `ga-f1frwf` (ctx-cancellable store reads to cut the `gc status` bd-read storm); related problem class #3888.

## Review notes

- `cmd/gc/bd_env.go`: the context-aware command runner keeps a single ctx-bound retry but intentionally does not run managed-Dolt recovery inside the status-read budget, and resolves env via no-recovery variants for the same reason (recovery can run under a 120s provider budget *before* the subprocess spawns). `bdStoreForCity`, `bdStoreForRig`, `controlBdStoreForCity`, and `controlBdStoreForRig` all wire `WithBdStoreRunnerContext`.
- `internal/beads/context_lister.go`, `internal/beads/bdstore.go`, `internal/beads/caching_store_reads.go`, `cmd/gc/bead_policy_store.go`: the optional-capability shape mirrors the existing optional `Counter` pattern instead of widening `Store.List`; each implementer carries a `var _ ContextLister` compile-time assertion so a signature drift fails the build instead of silently degrading to the non-cancellable path.
- `internal/api/handler_status.go`: `statusListStoreWithTimeout` runs both branches under one goroutine+select guard, bounding the caller even for ctx-ignoring `ListContext` implementations.
- No config, endpoint shape, or dashboard contract change is intended. The user-visible behavior change is bounded/cancellable status reads.
- The scoped-store files and API state hook are intentionally deleted because they were the earlier mitigation this implementation replaces.

## Scope: single feature (ContextLister)

The `GraphOnlyReadyStore` work an earlier revision bundled here has been dropped: those files were byte-identical to open PR #3853 ("Add GraphOnlyReadyStore support to beads store wrappers"), which is the feature's home, and they shipped no consumer here. This PR is now a single ContextLister theme. The prior `ga-yrna3v` release gate certified the superseded (bundled) commit, so it is removed; a fresh gate should be generated after re-review.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go build -tags gascity_native_beads ./...`; `go vet ./...` (both tags).
- [x] Full `internal/api`, `internal/beads` (native tag, real signals), and `internal/session` suites.
- [x] Production-construction-path child-kill proof for the new wiring: `GC_REAL_PROCESS_SIGNAL_TESTS=1 go test ./cmd/gc -run 'BdStoreForRigListContextKillsChildOnTimeout|ControlBdStoreForRigListContextKillsChildOnTimeout|BdStoreForCityListContextKillsChildOnTimeout'`.
- [x] Guard regression: `TestStatusListStoreWithTimeoutBoundsCtxIgnoringLister`. No-recovery env: `TestBdRuntimeEnvNoRecoveryDoesNotPublishProviderState`.
- [ ] Fresh release gate to be run post-re-review (prior gate removed with the de-bundled scope).

title: gc dolt health does not surface active compaction quarantine markers (silent until manual compact)
body:
## Summary

An active Dolt compaction quarantine marker (`.gc/runtime/packs/dolt/compact-quarantine/<db>`) blocks auto-GC and scheduled `gc dolt compact` for that database **indefinitely**, but there is no health/status signal that a quarantine is in effect. `gc dolt health` and `gc status` report nothing about it. A marker can sit for many days before anyone notices, while the un-GC'd database silently bloats.

This is a **detection/observability** gap that complements #2348 (which targets *preventing* benign-race quarantines, with #2350 proposing `LOCK TABLES` across the count window). Even with prevention in place, genuine quarantines (real value-hash drift, etc.) will still be created by design — and those should be **visible**, not silent. Defense in depth.

## Why this matters (incident background)

In a recent single-host multi-agent city, an `hq` quarantine marker (`reason=post-flatten row count decreased`) sat **~8 days** unnoticed. With GC/compaction blocked the whole time:

- the working-set `wisps` table grew to ~45k closed rows (~46k total) and `wisp_events` to ~300k rows;
- the store grew to ~1.4 GB for ~47k live rows;
- the controller and agents repeatedly run a full-partition scan of `wisps` (`SELECT id, content_hash, title, description, design, ... FROM wisps`), which pegged the managed `dolt sql-server` at 1–3 cores and saturated its connection pool (dropped connections, `unexpected EOF` / `invalid connection`, a connection-retry storm).
- The user-visible failure was that **new agent sessions could not start** (wedged in `start-pending → config`), and the only diagnostics were generic: `runtime status probe timed out` / `loading session snapshot timed out after 3s`. Nothing pointed at the quarantine.

The quarantine only became visible when an operator manually ran `gc dolt compact`, which printed the marker and mailed a controller alert. Clearing the marker + re-running compaction + purging stale wisps resolved it (store 1.4 GB → ~470 MB), confirming the data itself was fine — the harm was entirely from the **silent, long-lived** quarantine.

## Proposal

1. `gc dolt health` should scan `compact-quarantine/` and, when any marker exists, emit a clear **warning** line per quarantined DB (db, reason, age) and exit non-zero (or a warn-level status) so patrols/CI can catch it.
2. Ideally `gc status` surfaces a one-line warning too, and/or a periodic patrol raises an alert once a marker exceeds some age (e.g. a few hours), rather than only mailing on a manual compact attempt.

## Related observability gap (same command)

While confirming the above, the `Backups` line of `gc dolt health` reported `Backups: none found` even though periodic `mol-dog-backup` syncs were current (fresh artifacts under `.dolt-backup/<db>`). The health check appears to gauge backups by globbing `migration-backup-*` dirs only, ignoring the actual periodic backup artifacts — producing a misleading "none found". Worth fixing alongside, since both are `gc dolt health` giving a false sense of state.

## Environment

- `gc` 1.1.x, managed Dolt (single host, multiple active agents).

title: feat: add gc import check for cache/materialization validation
body:
## Problem

The Pack/City 0.13.6 import model assumes that normal city loads should not require live internet access once imports have been installed. Remote imports should resolve into local materialized state, with the lock file defining the desired resolved state.

That leaves a missing operational feature: users need a dedicated way to validate and repair import materialization when local cached/materialized content is missing or stale.

`gc doctor` is not the best home for this. This wants to live on the import surface itself.

## Proposed behavior

Add a new subcommand:

```text
gc import check
```

This command should validate the import installation state for the current city.

At a minimum it should:

- read the city's declared imports plus lock file
- verify that the required local materialized content exists
- check local cache availability before attempting network access
- explain clearly when an import is missing, stale, or cannot be materialized
- provide remediation guidance

Over time it could also support repair/rematerialization behavior.

## Intended import contract

This issue is also meant to lock in the intended behavior:

- normal load should not require internet access
- internet is required for fetch/update/rematerialization work
- the lock file is the authoritative statement of desired installed state
- missing materialized content should be repaired from local cache first, then remote source
- if repair is not possible, the user should get a clear actionable error

## Why this matters

- users reasonably expect installed imports to work offline
- docs need a precise story for local vs remote imports
- loader, package-manager, and UX need one consistent import contract

## Related docs/work

- migration guide work in `docs/guides/migrating-to-pack-vnext.md`
- import/cache/offline design note in local work products

title: gc prime: add --strict flag to error on unknown agents
body:
## Summary

`gc prime <name>` silently falls back to a generic default prompt when the agent doesn't exist. This is useful as a default behavior — any agent without a custom prompt gets a reasonable starting point. But when debugging, there's no way to distinguish "my agent's actual prompt" from "the fallback because I typo'd the name."

## Example

```
$ gc prime dfdfdf
# Gas City Agent

You are an agent in a Gas City workspace...
```

No error, no warning. If you're trying to verify your agent's prompt template renders correctly, this is a footgun.

## Proposal

Add a `--strict` flag that errors if the agent isn't found in the config:

```
$ gc prime dfdfdf --strict
Error: agent "dfdfdf" not found in city config
```

Without `--strict`, current behavior is preserved — the default prompt is returned for any agent.

title: Add PreCompact session cycling to all gastown pack overlays
body:
## Summary

- Create `overlays/default/.claude/settings.json` in both gastown and maintenance packs with a PreCompact hook that runs `gc handoff "context cycle"`
- Add the same PreCompact hook to the existing witness overlay
- Previously only the crew overlay had this; all other agents would just compact and keep running with degraded context

## Why

When Claude's context fills up, it triggers PreCompact. Without a session cycle hook, agents compact (lossy summarization) and continue with increasingly stale context — burning tokens on degraded reasoning that often needs to be redone.

Gas Town handled this with `gt handoff --cycle --reason compaction` in crew PreCompact hooks. This PR brings that behavior to all gastown pack agents.

Combined with `wake_mode=fresh` (PR #113), the full cycle is:
1. Context fills → PreCompact fires
2. `gc handoff "context cycle"` sends handoff mail + requests restart
3. Controller kills session, starts fresh (wake_mode=fresh clears session_key)
4. New session picks up from handoff mail with clean context

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify overlays are merged correctly into agent work dirs by the overlay system
- [ ] Trigger context compaction on a patrol agent, confirm it cycles instead of compacting
- [ ] Confirm handoff mail is delivered and new session resumes work
